title: rhun extension manifest (extension.ini), protocol version 1
description: The manifest is an INI file (UTF-8, key = value, # comments, unknown keys ignored). This schema describes it as the object it maps to: top-level keys are properties of the root; dotted keys such as run.linux-x86_64 become the 'run' object with the part after the dot as the key; each [section] is an object of the same name. Two rules the schema cannot state: 'name' must equal the folder's name and 'owner' the parent folder's name, and a target needs either a 'run' entry for it or 'runtime' with 'run'. Section 2 of v1.md says what each key means.

name.description: the extension's name, equal to its folder; commands are NAME.command

owner.description: the GitHub owner, equal to the parent folder

title.description: shown in Settings and after command titles

protocol.description: the protocol version this extension speaks

run.description: the program per target, relative to the extension folder (from the dotted keys run.TARGET); or, with 'runtime', the single key 'run' at the top level is the script

runtime.description: a program found on PATH that runs the script named by 'run' (python3, node, …)

requires.description: shown when the runtime is missing or too old; not checked by rhun 0.18.0

args.description: extra arguments for the program, space separated

on.description: when the extension starts: startup, command, project, lang:LANG, open:PATTERN; several, space separated; a manifest command always starts it

commands.description: [commands]: key = Title | default keys (space separated, each with a modifier; '|' and keys optional)

subscribe.description: [subscribe]: which events to send, with name patterns ('*' all, '*.go' a suffix, 'Makefile' an exact name, 'no' none); a document is reported only when 'opened' names it

needs.description: [needs]: the capabilities (section 5); a request without its capability is refused with 'needs'

run.description: programs the extension may start, by name, space separated

patterns.description: 'no', or space-separated name patterns: '*', '*.ext', an exact file name
